director.chapterArc: Callie begins by containing pain through breath, inventory, and routine. The journey widens into exposed, disorienting space, then becomes an exercise in adapting her tracking logic from lines to pools. Her enforced dependence—riding, remaining dry, yielding her mother’s hair to Ines—quietly strips away control while preserving competence. Pell’s validation restores a usable sense of identity just before the windmill turns hope into a resource trap: water is present, but five husks occupy the lowest ground.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder measured and observant. Pain is breath management, grief is inventory or surrendered work, and danger is spatial information. Let dry humor release pressure briefly without brightening the chapter. The final threat should narrow and cool the voice, not enlarge it; Duchess’s shaking carries the panic.

cues.delivery: A private diagnostic spoken to control the body; give each count weight without asking for sympathy.
cues.from: "Two ribs," she said to the underside of the wagon bed, not loud. "Three stitches. A finger of damp."
cues.through: "Two ribs," she said to the underside of the wagon bed, not loud. "Three stitches. A finger of damp."
cues.reason: Callie begins her breath-synced injury inventory under the wagon.

cues.delivery: Keep the dread buried inside exact counting; the repeated breaths are surveillance, not comfort.
cues.from: Her mother was asleep on the boards above her. Callie could hear her breathing through the planks. She listened to it the way she had listened to it every morning since Gaunt's Reach, in and out, in and out, and she let herself stop listening only when she had counted twenty.
cues.through: Her mother was asleep on the boards above her. Callie could hear her breathing through the planks. She listened to it the way she had listened to it every morning since Gaunt's Reach, in and out, in and out, and she let herself stop listening only when she had counted twenty.
cues.reason: Her mother’s breathing is the unspoken item in Callie’s inventory.

cues.delivery: Pell uses dry specification and impossible bravado to make a hard limit easier to accept; never play for a laugh.
cues.from: "On the flat." He took his hand away and wiped it on his coat. "At her pace, which is not my pace and it's not yours. An hour, and then she stands, and nobody argues with her about how long. No hills." He straightened, slowly, the way a man of sixty-one straightens. "If there's a hill between here and that light, I'll carry her up it myself, and I'd like it noted I said so before I'd seen it."
cues.through: "On the flat." He took his hand away and wiped it on his coat. "At her pace, which is not my pace and it's not yours. An hour, and then she stands, and nobody argues with her about how long. No hills." He straightened, slowly, the way a man of sixty-one straightens. "If there's a hill between here and that light, I'll carry her up it myself, and I'd like it noted I said so before I'd seen it."
cues.reason: His joke about carrying Duchess establishes authority and relieves pressure.

cues.delivery: Let Otto reason his way into the accidental insult with careful earnestness; he does not know he is being funny.
cues.from: "She looked at me all night. Every time I got up." He moved the arm in the new sling and seemed pleased with it. "I think that's good. I think she's decided I'm the one who's hers now." He thought about it. "I think she might have decided you're the one who isn't anything."
cues.through: "She looked at me all night. Every time I got up." He moved the arm in the new sling and seemed pleased with it. "I think that's good. I think she's decided I'm the one who's hers now." He thought about it. "I think she might have decided you're the one who isn't anything."
cues.reason: The humor comes from Otto’s literal conclusion about Duchess’s allegiance.

cues.delivery: Thick, weakened, and searching, but intelligible; her dry metaphor protects dignity while revealing that reality is slipping.
cues.from: "The barrow." Her mother shut her eyes. "No. You're right. The wagon." She lay still. "It was a barrow when I got hold of it and it turned into a wagon on the way out. That's the trouble with this morning. Everything's turning into something else on the way out."
cues.through: "The barrow." Her mother shut her eyes. "No. You're right. The wagon." She lay still. "It was a barrow when I got hold of it and it turned into a wagon on the way out. That's the trouble with this morning. Everything's turning into something else on the way out."
cues.reason: Callie’s mother recognizes and describes her own confusion.

cues.delivery: A tired mother gently catches Callie assessing her; place the wit precisely and keep concern underneath it.
cues.from: "You're doing sums on my face." Her mother did not open her eyes. "Don't do sums on my face, love. It's rude. Do them on Pell's, he likes it."
cues.through: "You're doing sums on my face." Her mother did not open her eyes. "Don't do sums on my face, love. It's rude. Do them on Pell's, he likes it."
cues.reason: She converts Callie’s alarm into a familiar domestic joke.

cues.delivery: Offer the memory as practical evidence for Callie to keep later; tenderness stays inside the instruction.
cues.from: "Good." Her mother's face did not change, but something went out of it that had been holding on. "Then it was worth what it cost. Remember I said so. I'll want you to have it written down, for when I'm cross about today."
cues.through: "Good." Her mother's face did not change, but something went out of it that had been holding on. "Then it was worth what it cost. Remember I said so. I'll want you to have it written down, for when I'm cross about today."
cues.reason: Her mother declares that seeing Callie survive was worth the physical cost.

cues.delivery: Katori’s protection arrives as cold arithmetic. Keep every clause flat, inevitable, and free of consolation.
cues.from: "You can walk," Katori agreed. "I watched you come out from under that wagon. You can walk about as well as Duchess can, and you'll walk yourself into a fever by the third day, and then I'll have two of you on the boards instead of one." She did not raise her voice. She never did. "So you're riding. Not on the bed. On the board, with Pell."
cues.through: "You can walk," Katori agreed. "I watched you come out from under that wagon. You can walk about as well as Duchess can, and you'll walk yourself into a fever by the third day, and then I'll have two of you on the boards instead of one." She did not raise her voice. She never did. "So you're riding. Not on the bed. On the board, with Pell."
cues.reason: Katori removes Callie’s choice in order to prevent further collapse.

cues.delivery: Widen the visual field and allow unease into the scale; this is exposure beneath something vast, not scenic wonder.
cues.from: And the sky came all the way down. That was what she could not get used to. On the flats there had been the scarp at the north edge, and on the road there had been banks and ditches and hedges to put a limit on things. Up here there was no limit. The sky came down to the grass on every side like a bowl turned over a plate, and the wagon crawled across the middle of the plate. It was the only moving thing in all that country. It made her feel as if something very large was looking down at it.
cues.through: And the sky came all the way down. That was what she could not get used to. On the flats there had been the scarp at the north edge, and on the road there had been banks and ditches and hedges to put a limit on things. Up here there was no limit. cues.reason: The limitless sky makes the wagon feel watched and terribly small.

cues.delivery: Treat the ash as measured loss, not nostalgia; let the final valuation land after the physical inventory.
cues.from: She did not mean to. She had gone to the barrow on the wagon bed for the bread, and the jar was there in its place under the flour, a screw-top jar with four Handfuls of ash in it. Next to the jar was Pell's tin with her name on it in his small neat hand. She did not need to open the tin. She knew what was in it. There was a grey film across the bottom and a little heap in one corner, less than a finger's worth. It was all that was left of the biggest thing she had ever owned.
cues.through: She did not mean to. She had gone to the barrow on the wagon bed for the bread, and the jar was there in its place under the flour, a screw-top jar with four Handfuls of ash in it. Next to the jar was Pell's tin with her name on it in his small neat hand. She did not need to open the tin. She knew what was in it. There was a grey film across the bottom and a little heap in one corner, less than a finger's worth. It was all that was left of the biggest thing she had ever owned.
cues.reason: Callie confronts what remains of the greatest resource she has owned.

cues.delivery: Keep Katori firm and unsentimental. The promise to teach is real, but it remains subordinate to keeping Callie alive.
cues.from: "Then it'll need you thinking, and that doesn't cost you anything." Katori finally looked at her. "I said I'd teach you the Edge properly. In daylight. On purpose. I haven't forgotten. I'll do it when you've got something in you to learn with, and not one day before, and you can be as cross with me about it as you like."
cues.through: "Then it'll need you thinking, and that doesn't cost you anything." Katori finally looked at her. "I said I'd teach you the Edge properly. In daylight. On purpose. I haven't forgotten. I'll do it when you've got something in you to learn with, and not one day before, and you can be as cross with me about it as you like."
cues.reason: Katori pairs refusal with a controlled promise of future instruction.

cues.delivery: Mother and daughter both preserve the other’s dignity: Callie insists from duty, and her mother refuses the sacrifice without pity.
cues.from: "Callie," she said quietly. "Don't."
cues.through: "I know you can. I'm asking you not to." Her mother did not turn round. "Ines."
cues.reason: Callie’s mother asks her to surrender a caregiving task she can no longer perform safely.

cues.delivery: Make the request exact and matter-of-fact; the catalogue of damaged hands is how she protects both women from embarrassment.
cues.from: "Would you do my hair," said Callie's mother. "My daughter's got a rib out of place and she's too proud to say so, and I've got a hand that's stopped taking instruction. And you've got two good ones, and you stitched her head yesterday without making a mess of it."
cues.through: "Would you do my hair," said Callie's mother. "My daughter's got a rib out of place and she's too proud to say so, and I've got a hand that's stopped taking instruction. And you've got two good ones, and you stitched her head yesterday without making a mess of it."
cues.reason: Callie’s mother recruits Ines without sentimentalizing their incapacity.

cues.delivery: Hold the loss in the simple act of watching; do not underline what this morning ritual meant to Callie.
cues.from: Callie sat on the ground by the wheel and watched somebody else do the thing she had said she would do in the mornings.
cues.through: Callie sat on the ground by the wheel and watched somebody else do the thing she had said she would do in the mornings.
cues.reason: Callie witnesses someone else assume the duty she claimed as hers.

cues.delivery: Ines states a specification, not a punchline; the dryness produces the humor.
cues.from: "Without any part left over," said Ines, and went back to her arrows.
cues.through: "Without any part left over," said Ines, and went back to her arrows.
cues.reason: Her shooting logic becomes an unexpectedly apt description of the braid.

cues.delivery: Let the small laugh open the door to contact, then keep the handclasp brief and almost intolerably restrained.
cues.from: Her mother laughed. It was a real laugh, small and tired. Then she looked down over the side of the tailboard at Callie, sitting against the wheel. She did not say anything. She put her left hand down over the edge of the boards, and Callie reached up and took it, and they held on for about three seconds, which was as long as either of them could stand.
cues.through: Her mother laughed. It was a real laugh, small and tired. Then she looked down over the side of the tailboard at Callie, sitting against the wheel. She did not say anything. She put her left hand down over the edge of the boards, and Callie reached up and took it, and they held on for about three seconds, which was as long as either of them could stand.
cues.reason: Mother and daughter permit themselves three seconds of direct tenderness.

cues.delivery: Pell validates Callie by analyzing her strategy, not praising her. Land the final distinction quietly: usefulness is not identity.
cues.from: "Because it's the one they'll want least." He moved the reins in his hands. "They'll want the other thing. The thing on the causeway, and the thing on the hill. Anybody would. And you've put the thing they don't want first, where they'll have to read it before they get to anything else." He glanced at her. "I've seen a great many people write down what they were at a great many gates, and most of them start with what they think the window's hoping for. You started with what you are."
cues.through: "Because it's the one they'll want least." He moved the reins in his hands. "They'll want the other thing. The thing on the causeway, and the thing on the hill. Anybody would. And you've put the thing they don't want first, where they'll have to read it before they get to anything else." He glanced at her. "I've seen a great many people write down what they were at a great many gates, and most of them start with what they think the window's hoping for. You started with what you are."
cues.reason: He recognizes that Callie has named what she is before naming what others want from her.

cues.delivery: Narrow from geographic deduction to visible bodies with clinical precision. Keep the counting controlled; certainty is the escalation.
cues.from: It was the lowest place in miles. Everything on the plain that drifted, sooner or later, drifted here.
cues.through: Callie counted them. She counted them twice, to be sure.
cues.reason: The hoped-for water source is revealed as the plain’s inevitable husk trap.

cues.delivery: A low field report with no flourish; the number alone changes the journey’s immediate problem.
cues.from: "Five," she said.
cues.through: "Five," she said.
cues.reason: Callie confirms the exact threat count.

cues.delivery: Make scarcity audible in the small slosh, then transfer the fear into Duchess’s body. End cold, quiet, and unresolved.
cues.from: Behind her on the wagon bed, a cask sloshed as the wheel went over a seam. It was a small sound, a cask with very little left in it. Duchess stood in the road with her head up and her nostrils wide, staring at the water, and began, very quietly, to shake.
cues.through: Behind her on the wagon bed, a cask sloshed as the wheel went over a seam. It was a small sound, a cask with very little left in it. Duchess stood in the road with her head up and her nostrils wide, staring at the water, and began, very quietly, to shake.
cues.reason: The remaining water and the mare’s trembling complete the trap.
